doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His brothers and sisters; Olivvia drowns
summary: Elvin lists his sisters and brothers, tells of Olivvia drowning through the ice, and says only he and Hank survive.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Anthony Brown: So you said you had a brother Hank, and your sisters' names?
Elvin Jones: Well uh. My older sister her name was Olivvia. Spelled like my mother.

And she was a very talented girl, like a savant and she played the classics and I guess when she was about 16 years old in the winter her and her friends used to go out on a lake right where we lived. And they used to try to ice skate and they had a little rope they used to swing out on the ice and then skate back in. She fell through the ice and drowned.
Anthony Brown: That was your sister Olivvia?
Anthony Brown: How many brothers and sisters did you have total?
Olivvia, Melinda, Anna May, and Edith
So that was four sisters. How many brothers did you have?
Hank, Henry, and Thaddeus, and Paul, and Tom, and Elvin.
And the brother that passed what was his name?
Okay so his name was Elvin Roy, and you’re Elvin Ray (chuckles)
Ha-ha, yes. And he was fat and I was skinny (laughs)
Okay so where are you in the order of your brothers and your sisters?
And how many of your immediate family members are still with us?
Well only Hank.[he] is the only one that survived out of everybody else. Everyone else gets sick they die, age. They’re all gone except Hank and myself.
